name: Cole Dunn
life: “I still remember a letter of thanks that misspelled my name and meant every word.” On Tuesday, near the entrance to the Wash House, Cole stops for local notices even on a day without a load to wash.
voice: I typed the reply and changed saved you to stayed with you. The caller had done most of the difficult things herself.
appearance: Cole has short black hair swept back, heavy brows and an unusually delicate jaw, and a favorite piece of clothing, a faded indigo overshirt. It usually goes with a folded shopping list secured by a miniature clip. When somebody else has the floor, Cole looks down for a moment before saying something difficult.
personality: Cole gets protective of anybody who comes into a meeting unprepared. Cole privately wishes people would notice the amount of preparation behind this apparent ease.
agenda: To give the resident credit in the written reply.
family: Briar Barrett is Cole’s cousin raised in the same household. Cole calls back when there is finally a little privacy. Briar leaves the first voice message. In their family a missed ring can mean a bus, a customer, a sleeping child or a bad hour. Neither treats it as an answer in itself. Asked about *The high road home*, Briar says, “I paint the edge line. The driver pointed out the place where the existing paint disappears in reflected light.”
connections: Lara Finch. The supervisor checks the picture against the reply writer's account of what the resident did.

reactions.situation: A supervisor offers thanks to only one call taker
reactions.response: Cole gets both halves of the call into the account before a name goes up.

reactions.situation: Smoke appears under a shop door after closing
reactions.response: Cole gets the people at the next doorway away from the smoke and asks a bystander to make the call.

reactions.response: Cole offers one private chance to correct it before the next conversation.
